values.meaning: Consider individual animals and their habitat needs, including less visible groups.
values.why: Restoration affects animals using the burned habitat
values.concern: Restoration organisations and field staff may unintentionally disturb shelter, feeding, movement or breeding.
values.requirement: Show likely effects on shelter, food, movement and breeding habitat
values.feature: Four explicit welfare dimensions in each pathway and AI assessment
values.evaluation: Check all four dimensions are assessed as conditional hypotheses or explicitly unknown; verify with field surveys.

values.meaning: Restore locally appropriate habitat functions without assuming more intervention is better.
values.concern: Land managers need locally suitable regeneration, habitat structure and erosion responses.
values.requirement: Compare effects on habitat structure and regeneration
values.feature: Three restoration options, spectral evidence and field checks
values.evaluation: Check vegetation, structure, regeneration and soil/erosion needs; do not interpret NDVI as ecosystem recovery by itself.

values.meaning: Make evidence, methods and assumptions inspectable.
values.concern: Ecologists, agencies and funders cannot independently evaluate unsupported explanations.
values.feature: Source-linked factual panels, structured evidence fields and report methodology
values.evaluation: Trace each factual AI item to a server-owned source field; inspect methods, assumptions and licences.

values.meaning: Keep missing data and the limits of inference visible.
values.concern: Landowners need usable guidance while researchers need sampling biases and unknown impacts disclosed.
values.requirement: Display evidence quality and flag the need for field validation
values.feature: Unknown labels, GBIF coverage warnings, uncertainty and survey requirements
values.evaluation: Check incomplete sampling, dates, spatial uncertainty and absent evidence are flagged; no absence or recovery claims from occurrence counts.

values.meaning: Humans must review and justify decisions; an AI draft cannot grant authority.
values.concern: Organisations, managers and public agencies need a clear responsibility and approval trail.
values.feature: Explicit review status, decision justification and approval checklist; no execution capability
values.evaluation: Block a locally recorded reviewed decision unless reviewer, rationale, preferred option and confirmation exist; always retain external approval requirements.

stakeholders.needs: Traceable evidence, animal welfare checks and defensible recovery options.
Feasible decisions, timing, habitat function and explicit responsibilities.
Understandable survey requirements, disturbance precautions and escalation.
Transparent progress and justified spending without oversimplified outcome scores.
Methodology, approval requirements and accountable human decisions.
Attribution, data quality, privacy and reproducible comparisons.

tensions: Rapid restoration versus avoiding wildlife disturbance: investigate breeding and refuge use before scheduling work.
Detailed biodiversity evidence versus protecting sensitive locations: retain aggregate evidence while withholding coordinates.
Simple recommendations versus communicating uncertainty: provide concise options and expandable limitations, not a single ethical score.
AI convenience versus expert accountability: retain human justification and approval requirements even when a model suggests an option.
